optics.calibration_status: User-supplied rgb.right K and resolution; KB4 distortion interpretation and robot-to-E6 mount remain provisional.

calibration.distortion_interpretation: OpenCV fisheye / Kannala-Brandt k1,k2,k3,k4; final four source entries are zero padding. Vendor model still unconfirmed.
calibration.extrinsics_reason: Unknown source reference frame, transform direction and quaternion order; source extrinsics are not known robot-link transforms.

optics.mount_estimate: Provisional external E6 right-eye location above/in front of the CAD head, inferred from stored real E6 imagery. Relative to the previous built-in optical frame: world displacement [+0.08,-0.033,+0.18] m at the fixed workcell pose. Not a measured hand-eye transform.
Optical center, aim and roll are provisional. Roll follows physical-side raw snapshot convention, not the 180-degree standalone review screenshots.
optics.view_target_note: Nominal optical axis aimed at the grasp volume; not a measured hand-eye transform.
optics.calibration_status: Circular fisheye appearance estimated from user-selected real inference frames; image-circle boundary fitted, 180-degree equidistant FOV assumed. Not a measured optical or hand-eye calibration.

calibration.rotation_evidence: VLA runtime uses decoded RGB without rotation; standalone screenshot tool has a different 180-degree review convention.
calibration.unapplied_reason: No evidence tying the ctrl calibration to the two independent wrist UVC sensors.
calibration.roll_reference: Stored physical-v2 raw wrist snapshots: left palm on the right, right palm on the left; optical roll estimate, not post-capture pixel rotation.
calibration.historical_topic_mapping_note: Full archive reviewed: 21 old mapping requests are excluded from this fit; 720 requests across 47 sessions match current physical left=camera3, right=camera1. Early image orientation differs; original files and names remain unchanged.
calibration.intrinsics_definition: fx=ellipse_radius_x/(pi/2), fy=ellipse_radius_y/(pi/2), principal point=image-circle center. Boundary is estimated in pixels; 180-degree angular FOV is an assumption.
